task_1.title: Avoid antivirus-related failures during package binary downloads
task_1.description: The update removes the atomic cache replacement step previously used when downloading package binaries and restores direct writes into the final cache layout. This reduces package download failures caused by Windows antivirus or file-locking interference while keeping incomplete downloads treated as non-ready cache entries.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that downloading a package binary into the local cache does not fail because publication of the downloaded package depends on an atomic replacement step that can be blocked by Windows antivirus or file locking. Ensure that interrupted or failed downloads are still treated as incomplete cache content rather than valid package binaries.

expectation.grounded: When Conan retrieves a package binary from a remote, it should create and populate the package's final cache layout directly and keep that layout under the existing dirty-package lifecycle during the download, instead of downloading to a separate temporary cache area and finalizing with os.replace. Users should no longer hit ConanException failures caused by the final os.replace step during package binary downloads, especially on Windows systems affected by antivirus scanning.
expectation.conceptual: Package downloads should complete reliably even when antivirus or other background software briefly interferes with file operations. A package should only appear usable in the cache once its download has completed, and failed downloads should remain clearly incomplete.

constraints.grounded: Do not require a separate temporary download directory or an atomic directory swap to publish downloaded package binaries into the cache. Preserve the existing dirty or incomplete state handling around package layouts so unsuccessful downloads do not become normal cached packages.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve reliability of package downloads without changing what a successful cached package means or allowing partial downloads to be mistaken for complete ones.

behavior: Package binaries fetched from remotes are written into their normal cache layout immediately instead of first being staged in a separate temporary download location.
Conan no longer relies on a final os.replace operation to make a downloaded package visible in the cache, removing that failure mode from package binary downloads.
The package layout remains in an incomplete or dirty state for the duration of the download and is only considered a normal cached package after the download finishes successfully.
Cache maintenance no longer needs to manage a dedicated temporary area that existed only for staged package binary downloads.
acceptance_criteria: When a package binary is downloaded from a remote on Windows, the download should not fail solely because a final atomic replacement of the package directory is blocked by antivirus or file locking.
When Conan downloads a package binary, it should populate the package's regular cache location directly rather than depending on a later publish step from a separate staging directory.
When a package download is interrupted or fails before completion, the resulting cache content should remain incomplete and should not be treated as a valid, ready-to-use package binary.
After the upgrade, package download behavior should no longer depend on a dedicated temporary download cache area for binary staging.
